deep.reconstruction:
This page is a bookkeeping table, not a mathematical derivation. It is headed 'Tertia' and has a row for each year from 1800 to 1834. Each row gives two money amounts, one under 'März' (March) and one under 'Sept.' (September). These are presumably two half-yearly payments or receipts, at Easter and Michaelmas. Each amount is written in the triple notation Thaler.Groschen.Pfennig (for example 122.10.8 = 122 Thaler, 10 gute Groschen, 8 Pfennig). The middle field never exceeds 23, which fits 24 Groschen to the Thaler with 12 Pfennig to the Groschen. In modern terms, an entry a.b.c equals 288a + 12b + c Pfennig, or a + b/24 + c/288 Thaler. Almost every Pfennig field is 0, 4 or 8, so the amounts are multiples of 1/3 Groschen. That suggests a sum divided into thirds or shares. The heading 'Tertia', a third share, fits this.

A third column holds small integers, mostly between 2 and 18. Its header next to 1800 is hard to read (perhaps 'Caffeng.' / 'Cassen'?), and the 1801 entry in it is a struck-out dash. These are probably counts of the events that generated the fees (persons, cases, promotions or similar). The sums do not appear to be simply proportional to them.

Two marginal annotations mark changes of currency standard. At 1821 there is a vertical stroke and 'Conv.' (Conventionsmünze). At 1834 there is a stroke and 'Court.' (Courant). From those dates the figures are presumably in a different coin standard, so the series is not homogeneous across those breaks.

The overall pattern is:
- amounts are low (about 100–200 Thaler per half-year) in 1800–1814;
- they rise to about 400–590 in 1822–1828;
- they fall back to about 200–290 by 1832–1834.

The series begins before Gauss came to Göttingen in 1807, so it was copied from official accounts. It is probably his share of some faculty or university fund, or data he gathered for actuarial or financial purposes. The neighbouring pages are likewise practical memoranda (mirror prices, post timetables, microscope measurements). No computation, totals or derivation appear on the page.
errors: 1813 March entry '140.22.9': a Pfennig value of 9 breaks the otherwise consistent pattern of 0/4/8. It is possibly a slip for 140.22.8, or a misreading.

Several entries are overwritten or corrected: the 1803 year label is written over 1802, the 1802 September amount (148?) is retouched, the 1831 September amount (229.0.4 or 229.10.4?) is heavily overwritten, and the 1833 year label and the March amount (198 or 193?) are retouched. No arithmetic is performed, so there are no computational errors to check.

results.what: Half-yearly (March/September) record of money amounts in Thaler.Groschen.Pfennig for 1800–1834, with a count column and notes on currency-standard changes (Conv. 1821, Court. 1834)
results.modern_name: financial record / time series of receipts (no mathematical content)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely administrative or financial table of half-yearly sums with no mathematics. It fits Gauss's well-known habit of compiling numerical records, including his work on university and widows'-fund finances.

checkable.asserts: The 1800 March entry 122.10.8 equals 35264 Pfennig (1 Thaler = 24 Gr = 288 Pf).
The 1800 annual total (March + September) is 272 Thaler 5 Gr 4 Pf (78400 Pf).
The March Pfennig fields (excluding the 1813 entry of 9) are all multiples of 4, i.e. the amounts are multiples of 1/3 Groschen.

transcription_corrections: Amounts are money in Thaler.Groschen.Pfennig (e.g. 122.10.8), not decimals.
Column header after the 1800 row is uncertain: reads like 'Caffeng.' / 'Cassen'; transcription 'Caffery' is doubtful.
1801 third column: a struck-out dash, not a value.
1802 September: '148.5.4' with the 148 overwritten or retouched.
1811 third column reads '13' (the stroke before it is part of the dash).
1831 September is heavily overwritten: '229.0.4' or possibly '229.10.4'.
1833: the year label is overwritten (1833 over another digit); the March amount '198.2.—' may have 198 written over 193.
